Letter from Chen Chi Mei 陳其美 to
Mr. Tung Yung Ching. 董榮卿 of the
Sin Kong Indigo Hong 新康顏料號

To Mr. Yung Ching.
My previous letter to you, I presume, you have noted.
The national affairs have become more critical. I hope you will speedily decide and support the Republican army to enable them to carry out their object to a successful issue. Not only myself will be fortunate. As long as there is war, business cannot improve. Not only is there no improvement but everything is at a standstill and bankruptcy or failure is a matter for consideration. If the thief Yuan is not removed you cannot enjoy peace nor can you carry on business as usual. Note the condition of L-sha 白沙, Szechuen and Hunan where the Northern soldiers commit rape, robbery and other inhuman offences. I feel pity for these poor people who have suffered through the tyrant.
If you wish to protect yourself, your property, your wife, your sons, why don't you assist us? The rich should open their purses and the poor help us with their strength. If the people decide without hesitation, the thief will certainly be overthrown. Don't follow the steps taken in 1913 when assistance was rendered (by the merchants) to the tyrant. This resulted in endless trouble in China and in the calamities which you are now suffering. For the sake of yourself and your sons and grandsons, you should not repeat helping Yuan. You are quite intelligent and you must know what is right now. Besides risking my life, I have devoted myself to national affairs. Why? Because I cannot bear to view the situation. I am not working for self interest. This you well know. The big movement now going on is not a risk for the Revolutionaries. Because the guilt of the wicked thief (or traitor) is well known, our party have thoroughly prepared to take this course. The Yunnan and Kweichow army alone is strong enough to fight with the enemy. There are additional forces from the Yangtze and Northern provinces which will make the loss (of Yuan's Government) most certain. If I had not had the situation well in hand I would not wish to waste your money and I would not wish to lose my confidence. During the past 2 years I have depended only on contributions from emigrants abroad and have not made any request to you. Now that success is imminent, I therefore wish you to share the difficulties in order that peace may be restored earlier. If the war is prolonged, not only the people will suffer, it is feared that foreigners will make aggressions and cause danger or loss to the country. I always respect civil rights. What I want is a public loan and not a private contribution. Moreover regulations of rewards have been clearly drawn up and receipts for the loan will be returned if desired. On the day of success, the exact amount of money will be returned without fail. In view of this, it will be seen that if you contribute a portion of the surplus of your business profit, the nation will be saved and you will not suffer any loss. To be kind is a policy everyone should adopt. Why should you hesitate? and why should you fear? Why should the animal-like and inhuman Northern troops to trample on the Southern region, deteriorate the land and cause the people to submit to death without being able to resist. You are not ignorant and surely you will not act as stated above. I appeal to you on behalf of the people. So I take the trouble of repeating the above advice. I hope you will listen to me. The dangers that confront us at present cannot be described in a few words. Please ponder and favour me with a reply as soon as possible.

(sd) Chen Chi Mei.
(sealed). -de-

荣卿先生台鉴：
前函谅已察悉。国事日益危急，望速作决断，支持共和军，使其目标得以顺利实现。此举不仅本人幸甚。只要战事不息，商业便无法好转。非但无起色，且万事停滞，破产或倒闭皆在考量之中。若不除去袁贼，则不得安宁，亦无法正常经商。请看白沙、四川及湖南等地状况，北兵在那里实施强奸、抢劫及其他无人道之罪行。吾对这些受暴君之苦的可怜百姓深表同情。
若欲保护自身、财产、妻儿，何不助我一臂之力？富者解囊，贫者出力。若民众毫不犹豫作出决定，袁贼必被推翻。切勿重蹈1913年商民援助暴君之覆辙。此举导致中国无尽之麻烦，以及你们目前正遭受的灾难。为了你自己及子孙后代计，不应再次帮助袁氏。你素来聪慧，定知当下何为正道。我除冒生命危险外，更投身于国事。为何？因不忍目睹此局势。我并非为一己私利工作，此点你深知。当前之大运动对革命党人而言并非冒险。因奸贼（或叛徒）之罪行众所周知，我党已为此行动做好充分准备。仅云南和贵州军队之力便足以与敌军作战。另有来自长江流域及北方各省之援军，将使（袁政府之）失败成为定局。若我对局势没有十足把握，便不会愿浪费你的钱财，也不愿失去我的信誉。过去两年，我仅依赖海外侨胞之捐款，未向你提出任何请求。如今成功在即，故望你能分担困难，以便早日恢复和平。若战事延长，不仅百姓受苦，恐外人亦将趁机侵略，给国家带来危险或损失。我一向尊重民权。我所求者为公债，而非私人捐赠。此外，奖励章程已明确制定，如有需要，可退还借据。成功之日，所借款项必将如数归还。由此可见，若你捐出部分营业利润之余款，既可救国，你又不会蒙受损失。行善乃人人应采纳之方针。你为何犹豫？又为何恐惧？怎能让如禽兽般无人道的北军践踏南方地区，破坏土地，致使百姓无力抵抗而任人宰割。你并非无知之人，想必不会如上所述行事。我代表民众向你呼吁。故我不厌其烦，重申上述建议。望你能听从我的意见。目前我们面临的危险非寥寥数语所能描述。请深思并尽快赐复。

（签名）陈其美
（盖章）。-de-

Regulations of the Bureau for raising contributions.
Art.1. The establishment of the Bureau for raising
contributions and the locality where it is situated should
be decided by special deputies from the Ministry...
(Ministry of Finance of the Chinese Kou ming Tang..
as the seal on the paper shows)..
Art.2 The personell of the Bureau are:-
1 Chief manager
1 Superintandent ..
A committee comprised of several members, one of whom
will audit the accounts..
1 Secretary..
1 treasurer..
Art.3 the Chief manager shall be appointed on the recommendation
of the special envoy of this Ministry or nominated by the
President of a branch society and his appointment confirmed
by this Ministry..
Art.4 The Superintendent shall be chosen from among the
Presidents of branch societies but in places where there is
no branch society and where the President of a branch society
has assumed office as Chief manager, the candidate for the
appointment shall be nominated by the local members..
Art.5. The subordinate staff under the manager shall be..
elected by the members..
Art.6. After the Bureau has been established, the manager
shall report the names, age, native place and occupations
of his subordinate staff, to the Ministry..
Article 7.. The Bureau on receiving contributions will
issue receipts in the name of the Bureau , to the
contributor.. At the same time it will forward to the
Ministry an account of the amount received and a full
statement of the contributions in order that Debenture Bonds
may be issued and an Order of Merit be conferred on the
contributor according to regulations.
The Bureau upon receipt of the Debenture Bonds, and Orders
of Merit will give them to the contributor in exchange for
the receipts given to them in the first instance which
will then be destroyed..
Article 8. The Bureaux for raising contributions will be..
dissolved after the revolution has been brought to a successful
issue and after the loan has been refunded..

Regulations regarding rewards in return for contributions.
No.1 No matter the amount of the contributions to the
revolution, they will be refunded to the owner two fold in..
adherence with the procedure of the first revolution..
The payment of principal together with interest will be..
made within 3 years after the success of the revolution..
No.2 Those who contribute $100 will be rewarded with the
Order of Merit of the 3rd Class.. When decorated with this
Order they will be permitted to enjoy the privileges of..
citizenship although they are not members of this party..
No.3 Those who contribute $1000 will be rewarded with the
Order of Merit of the 2nd Class.. Decorated with this Order
they will have the following privileges:-
1. Like a member of this party they will enjoy the right of
citizenship.
2. They will have the special right to undertake mining..
and other industrial work.
No.4. Those who contribute $10,000 will be awarded with the
Order of Merit of 1st Class.. They will have the following
privileges:-
a. Special right in mining and industrial undertakings.
b. Recognised by the Government as a representative of the..
Citizens and permitted to participate in political affairs
and in Parliament organisations..

Regulations governing the decoration. .
1. The decorations of Orders of Merit are solely for the
purpose of encouraging contributions. .
2. Orders of Merit are divided into 3 classes. .
1st class made of gold. .
2nd " silver. .
3rd " brass. .
3. The shape of the order will be round , one inch in
diameter. . On the face will be a sun with 12 rays. .
The class will be marked on the reverse side and underneath
it will be inscribed a tree. .
4. There will be a white ribbon with red edges attached to
the badge of the order. This ribbon will be 1 3/4" long and
1 7/10" broad. . The edge will be 2/10 of an inch broad. .
5. The order shall be worn on the left breast. .
6. Persons decorated will be allowed to wear the order
through their lives. .
7. The names of the wearers of decorations will be
kept by the society in a secret and safe manner in order
that the record may be handed over to the Mint Bureau
later on. .

Regulations regarding the issue of Debenture Bonds. .
Artl. The payment and return of Debenture Bonds shall be
made in Japanese gold coins. . Contributions from the
interior and treaty ports to be made in Japanese money
according to the rate of exchange as shown in Article 2.
Art.2. Debenture bonds are divided into 3 kinds, viz:
$10,$100,and $1,000. . They will be given to the
contributors in exchange for the money contributed. .
If the amount received does not exceed $10, the Board
of Finance will record the contribution and the
name of the contributor, and wait until further contributions
to reach $10 before a debenture Bond is issued. .
Art.3 The interest on the loan will be the same amount
as mentioned on the Debenture Bond. .
Art.4. The 3 kinds of Debenture Bonds will be redeemed
within 3 years after the establishment of the Republican
Government at a date to be appointed by the Board of
Finance. .

To Mr. Wei Ching,

A long time has elapsed since I last
communicated with you. I have not yet received a reply
to the request which I made to you last year. I think
you being a rich man in China, do not wish to make
friends with the poor. There is now a very good
opportunity for me to act. Such an opportunity has not
been found since the birth of the Revolution. Therefore
I write to request you to help by sending a small sum
of money which can be saved from the toilet expenses
of your family but which will enable our party to bring
a movement to a successful issue. If you grant this
favour, I shall be ever grateful.
Last year it is said, you contributed some money.
I have never seen it. Yu Ya Ching must have put the
money into his own pocket. My friend Sun Siau Poo
has from time to time supplied me with sums amounting
to $300. Apart from this, I have received nothing.
All our communications are private. You should not
discuss this affair with Yu Ya Ching or pass anything
to him. If you do so, I will take no heed of you.
The men under my control are very angry and if they
ascertain you have handed the money to Yu Ya Ching,
any action taken by them is beyond expectation. I
hope you will at once see your relative Mr. Zee Ping
Sun 徐 臣 and request him to communicate with Mr.
Li 李 of the Butterfield & Swire and settle with them
in order to spare me the trouble of warning my subordinates
against taking steps. This is very important.

With compliments.
(sd) Shu Tsung Au.

致魏清先生：

自上次与您通信以来，已过去很长时间。我去年向您提出的请求，至今未获回复。我想您身为中国富人，大概不愿与穷人结交。如今我有一个极好的行动机会。自革命爆发以来，尚未出现过这样的良机。因此，我写信请求您施以援手，寄来一笔小款，这笔钱可从您家庭的日常开销中节省出来，但足以使我党将一项运动推向成功。若您肯赐予此恩惠，我将感激不尽。

据说去年您曾捐助过一些款项。但我从未见过这笔钱。虞洽卿（Yu Ya Ching）定是将钱装进了自己的腰包。我的朋友孙筱圃（Sun Siau Poo）不时向我提供总计300元的款项。除此之外，我分文未收。

我们所有的联络均属私密。您不应与虞洽卿讨论此事，也不应将任何物品转交给他。若您这样做，我将不再理会您。我手下的人非常愤怒，若他们查明您已将钱交给虞洽卿，他们所采取的行动将出乎意料。我希望您立即去见您的亲戚徐臣（Zee Ping Sun）先生，并请他与怡和洋行（Butterfield & Swire）的李（Li）先生联系并与其结清账目，以免我去警告我的下属采取行动。此事至关重要。

此致
敬礼

（签名）舒宗敖（Shu Tsung Au）。

附件一份。

如有回复，请寄给怡和洋行进口航运部会计师李传文（Li Wei Wen）先生。

--------------------------

（签名）舒宗敖（Shu Tsung Au）。

江苏共和军总司令。

page_data.en:
Translation of a letter from Shu Tseng Ah 许震亞
to Mr. Chiu Zung Ching 邱润卿 of Ta Chong
Hong 德昶号 in the Ting Shin Li 鼎新里
alleyway, Kiukiang Road, date on envelope 15th
of the 1st month.

To Mr. Zung Ching,
I have written several letters to
you but have received no reply. On Chinese new
year's eve, I met my partisan Sung Ziang Foo 孙祥夫
who advised me to deal with you gentlemen in a modest
manner. In view of the difficult position of the
nation and the weakness of our party, I understand
that it is impossible to obtain your assistance by
using force and therefore prefer to show humility.
Presuming that you do not like flattery, I have
made the requests which are neither strong nor
humble. But to my surprise, you have not given any
reply for reasons unknown to me.
Many persons have said that you have already
lent out some money which has been misappropriated
by me. This untrue story has, to my regret, badly
damaged my reputation and has become unbearable to
me. Laying aside my worthless requests for a loan,
I now again write to you to enquire as to whom you
paid the money, and if you did pay someone, I cannot
bear the responsibility. I do not care whether you
will assist me and give a reply or not, but this is
the last letter to end the affair. Hereafter we will
not be enemies. Someday in the future we will meet
and talk together. This is the spring season and
the weather is getting warm. I wish you to take
care of your health.

(sd) Shu Tseng Ah. 许震亞

13th day 1st mon

许震亚（Shu Tseng Ah）致九江路鼎新里德昶号邱润卿（Chiu Zung Ching）先生信函之译文，信封日期为正月十五日。

致润卿先生：

我曾给您写过几封信，但未收到回复。除夕之夜，我遇见了我的党人孙祥夫（Sung Ziang Foo），他建议我以谦恭的态度与诸位先生打交道。鉴于国家处境艰难以及我党力量薄弱，我明白使用武力无法获得您的协助，因此宁愿示以谦卑。 presuming 您不喜欢阿谀奉承，我提出的请求既不强硬也不卑微。但令我惊讶的是，出于我不明原因，您未作任何答复。

许多人说您已经借出了一些钱，而被我挪用了。这种不实之辞遗憾地严重损害了我的声誉，令我难以忍受。暂且放下我这微不足道的借款请求，我现在再次写信给您，询问您将钱付给了谁；如果您确实付给了某人，我无法承担此责任。我不在乎您是否会协助我并给予回复，但这将是结束此事的最后一封信。此后我们将不再是敌人。将来某日我们会见面交谈。正值春季，天气渐暖。祝您保重身体。

（签名）许震亚（Shu Tseng Ah）。

正月十三日

page_data.en:
To Mrs. Wei Ching.,

I have addressed many letters to you
but have not received any reply. . I can neither understand
the reason nor your idea. . I do not know why you despise
me. . I recollect that the words I used for borrowing money
from you were not at all strong and the representative
I sent to you was not a man of low class. . I do not know
why you are so obstinate in refusing to give a reply
from first to last. . Is it because you have money so you
can make friends with Yuan or is it because you have
property which God will help you to keep? I do not care
for this, but I now allow you three days commencing from
to-day within which to send the money which I have asked
for to the care of Mr. Li Wei Hung 李信文 , the
accountant of the Import Shipping Office of Butterfield
& Swire. . This will save the lives of your family and
save your property, otherwise not only the lives of the
members of your family but also those of your employees
may be endangered. . Please ponder and ponder well.

With Compliments. .

(sd) Shu Tsung Au. .

Morning of the 15th of the 2nd moon. .

P.S.
This is private dealing between you and I and if. .
you tell others about it, I will not give up until the
lives of all the members of your family have been taken. .
You will then appreciate my power. .

Envelope.
Mrs. Chiu Wei Ching. .
The Ta Cheng Hong. .
Ting Shing Li alleyway
Kiukiang Road. .

Name mentioned inside. .

Rough translation of a letter from one Hsu Tseng Ah
to Mr. Chiu Wei Ching:-

To Mr. Wei Ching,
Owing to the pressing need of money to
cope with the situation I have repeatedly sent letters
and representatives to request you most humbly for
assistance but so far you have given me no reply.
This has placed me in a state of distress and I am
unable to find any other person to whom I can appeal.
I don't know what to do now. The situation of Szechuan
and Kwangtung is worse nor there is any hope for any
of the southern part of China. You confine yourself
in your house and fail to give a definite reply which
will cause danger in future and will seriously effect
the Republicans. Although you have millions of property
how can you enjoy yourself.
Now I again write this letter and forward it to
you through Mr. Li of Butterfield and Swire.
Will you kindly reconsider my previous request
and send the money through Mr. Li in order to enable
us to respond immediately to the appeal of Kweichow
and Yunnan and to enlarge the influence of our party.
Further developments will be fortunate, the citizens
will be fortunate and you and myself will also be
fortunate.
Please reply at once through Butterfield & Swire.
(signed) Hsu
(Seal) Hsu Tseng Ah.

Envelope.
Mr. Chiu Wei Ching,
Ta Cheng Indigo Heng.
To be delivered by Butterfield & Swire.

徐某（Hsu Tseng Ah）致邱渭清（Chiu Wei Ching）先生信函之大意译文：

致渭清先生：

由于急需资金以应对局势，我多次派遣信件和代表，极其谦卑地请求您给予援助，但至今您未给我任何回复。这使我陷入困境，且找不到其他可以求助的人。我现在不知如何是好。四川和广东的局势更糟，中国南方任何地方都没有希望。您闭门不出，不给予明确答复，这将导致未来的危险，并严重影响共和党人。虽然您拥有百万家产，但您怎能安心享受。

现在我再次写此信，并通过怡和洋行的李先生转交给您。

恳请您重新考虑我之前的请求，并通过李先生寄送款项，以便我们能够立即响应贵州和云南的呼吁，并扩大我党的影响力。若事态进一步发展顺利，则是公民之幸，也是您我之幸。

Rough translation of letter from one Wong Teh Ming
to Mr. Pao Yuen Sung.

As we have called several times at your residence,
seeking an interview without success and we think
you are always busy.
Owing to the failure of the recent Chacho incident
forty two of us have remained in Shanghai and are in
very poor circumstances, as support from our party
is not forthcoming. A day to us is as a year.
We therefore write and request you to lend us $2000
to defray our expenses in travelling to Yunnan.
On our arrival at that destination, we will return
the money you. As soon as we succeed we will try
our best to return our appreciation for your help.
As you are a well known merchant in Shanghai being
generous and intelligent, it is hoped you will
not refuse to end such a small sum of money.
We are human beings, and are quite different
from grass and wood which have no feelings at all.
We naturally will be grateful to you if you will
save us from difficulties. If you do not know
what is right and persist in refusing to give
us the money we will take steps which will cause
you to end your life in the same way as Chang
Si Yen did.
On receipt of this letter please make the necessary
preparations, our deputy will call at 10 o'clock
on the 28th for the money.
Fearing that you may regard this letter as idle
talk and take no notice of it we forward herewith
a badge belonging to our party. You should not
regard us as robbers, you must keep the badge in
a sealed envelope and return to us through bearer
on the 28th together with your reply and money.
With compliments.

(sd) Wong Teh Ming and others.

Envelope.
Mr. Pao Yuen Sung,
Pae Kung Kwan,

Frenchtown.

因我们数次前往府上拜访，求见未果，想必您总是繁忙。

由于近期查扣事件失败，我们四十二人滞留上海，境况十分窘迫，因为我党支援未到。度日如年。

因此，我们写信请求您借给我们2000元，以支付前往云南的路费。抵达目的地后，我们将归还款项。一旦成功，我们将尽力回报您的帮助。

您是上海知名的商人，慷慨且明智，希望您不要拒绝出借这样一笔小款。

我们是人，与毫无感情的草木截然不同。若您能将我们从困境中解救出来，我们自然会对您感激涕零。若您不明是非，坚持拒绝给我们这笔钱，我们将采取步骤，使您像张士燕（Chang Si Yen）那样结束生命。

收到此信后，请做好必要准备，我们的副手将于28日10点钟前来取款。

恐您视此信为戏言而不予理会，现随信附上我党徽章一枚。您不应将我们视为强盗，请将徽章装入密封信封，并于28日连同您的回复和款项交由来人带回。

page_data.en:
Rough translation of a letter dated 8th February
from the Shanghai Office of the Chinese Republican
Army to Mr. Pe Yuen Sung 贝润生 , Ex Admiral
Sayle.

To
Mr. Peen Sung,
A new year has come. The Globe has
turned round once more. We wish you happiness and
long life. You are as bright as the new year. Your
whole family are rejoicing at the approach of the
spring. But the national affairs are still unsettled.
Yunnan and Kweichow have risen and large military
funds are needed. As the land is unproductive,
produce is scarce and the people are poor. The
extraction of wealth by the wicked Government during
the past few years has been unremitting. The people
are consequently in a dangerous position. This
Army observing on behalf of Heaven the pitiful
condition of the people, will by no means ill-treat or
and increase the burden of their brethren. Therefore
we are obliged to have recourse to rich places.
You know very well there were patriotic persons in
every dynasty who showed their good qualities when
the nation got into trouble. You are kind hearted
person and you have a clear conception of the present
situation. So far as national affairs are concerned
you have already an idea in you head as to how to
save the nation from the dangers with which she is
threatened, as a good citizen of a Republic should,
and there is no need for me to expostulate further.
Owing to the critical situation and the urgent
requests for military funds, we are reluctantly
compelled to ask you for $500,000 to be used in
Szechuen and Kwangsi. In future if the great affair
proves successful and if the wicked devils are
driven out, all the citizens will be grateful to
you. We cannot say anything more in this letter
and ask you the favour of your immediate reply.

With new year greetings.

Dated 8th February.

(Sealed) The Shanghai Office of the
Chinese Republican Army.

（印：中华共和军上海机关之印）
page_data.zh:
中华共和军上海机关于2月8日致前拜尔上将、贝润生（Pe Yuen Sung）先生信函之大意译文。

致
贝松（Peen Sung）先生：

新年伊始。地球又转了一圈。祝您幸福长寿。您如新年般光明。您全家正为春天的到来而欢欣。但国事仍未安定。云南和贵州已起义，需要大量军费。由于土地贫瘠，物产稀缺，百姓贫困。过去几年，邪恶政府不断搜刮财富。因此，人民处于危险境地。本军仰观天意，怜悯百姓疾苦，决不会虐待或增加同胞的负担。因此，我们不得不向富庶之地寻求资助。

您很清楚，每个朝代都有爱国之士，在国家危难之时展现其优良品质。您是一位心地善良的人，对当前局势有清晰的认识。就国事而言，作为一名共和国的好公民，您心中已有如何将国家从面临的危险中拯救出来的想法，无需我再多加劝诫。

由于局势危急且急需军费，我们被迫无奈向您索要50万元，用于四川和广西。将来若大业成功，驱逐了邪恶魔鬼，全体公民都将感激您。信中不便多言，恳请您立即回复。

顺颂
新禧

2月8日。

（盖章）中华共和军上海机关。

（印：中华共和军上海机关之印）

page_data.en:
Translation of a letter signed by Wong Kou Wah 王國華
and Tsu Ming Sung 朱夢松 to Pao Yuen Sung 包潤生
Rue Animal Bayle.

Sir,
Although we are strangers to you, we wish to
take this opportunity of offering you our best wishes
for your happiness and success in business.
With reference to your remittance of $50,000
through the Yokohama Specie Bank (? to whom not
mentioned), we realise your generosity and
your warm interests in public welfare.
We are fully aware that apart from being
a leading merchant you are deeply interested
in charitable business and all the gentry,
merchants and educationalists respect you.
Having stayed here for a long time we are in
a great need of money to defray expenses,
and as the year is drawing to an end,
we can neither borrow nor ask for remittances
from home.
We therefore request you to lend us $10,000
in order to enable us to return to our native place.
As soon as we can improve our condition to some
extent we will refund the money with interest.
We will not fail to do so. If you are willing
to comply with our request please send us
the money in bank notes properly wrapped
in newspapers in order to prevent outsiders
knowing the contents. Thus you will avoid any
future annoyance of other people who may call
for money. If others know they will want same also.
So it is better that we should both keep
the matter secret especially for your sake.
We should have called on you personally
had it not been for the prevalence of robberies
and murders at present.
Our presence may cause surprise and alarm among
the members of your family. The request for
a loan from pure strangers seems unreasonable
and unusual but you should know that you may
receive in return a reward far better than the
gift with which you favour us.
You may not believe us now but you will see
the result in future.
As we have assured you most frankly, it is
hoped that you will give us a bigger loan
than we have asked for. We trust you will
not disappoint us.
We will come for the article in three days
time. If you refuse to do what is requested,
please tell us.

With compliments.

Wong Kou Wah.
Tsu Ming Sung.

22nd day of the 12th moon.
page_data.zh:
王国华（Wong Kou Wah）与朱梦松（Tsu Ming Sung）致包润生（Pao Yuen Sung）信函译文，地址：贝勒路（Rue Animal Bayle）。

先生：

虽与您素不相识，但我们愿借此机会向您致以最良好的祝愿，祝您幸福及生意兴隆。

关于您通过横滨正金银行汇出的五万美元（收款人未提及），我们感念您的慷慨以及对公共福利的热切关注。

我们深知，您不仅是一位杰出的商人，还深切热衷于慈善事业，所有士绅、商人和教育家都对您敬重有加。

我们在此滞留已久，急需资金支付开销，且因年关将至，既无法借贷，也无法向家乡请求汇款。

因此，恳请您借给我们一万美元，以便我们能够返回故乡。一旦我们的境况稍有好转，定将连本带利归还。我们绝不食言。若您愿意应允我们的请求，请将钞票用报纸妥善包裹后寄给我们，以防外人知晓内情。这样可避免日后其他人前来索款给您带来烦恼。若他人知晓，也会同样索要。因此，最好是我们双方对此事保密，尤其是为了您的利益着想。

若非目前抢劫和谋杀案频发，我们本应亲自登门拜访。我们的出现可能会引起您家人的惊讶和恐慌。向完全陌生的人提出借款请求似乎不合情理且不寻常，但您应当知道，作为回报，您获得的奖赏将远胜于您赐予我们的这份厚礼。

您现在或许不信，但将来定会看到结果。

正如我们要坦率地向您保证的那样，希望您能给予比我们所求数额更大的贷款。相信您不会让我们失望。

我们将在三天后来取物品。若您拒绝所请，请告知我们。

此致

王国华
朱梦松

腊月二十二日

October 14th

Sir,
Chen Che May 陳其美 was reported by the Police as being in the French Concession in the month of November 1915. He had been seen in the house of the late Wang Ching Fah 王金發 where he was trying to obtain a loan of $30,000.
In the beginning of the month of December 1915 he was staying in a house on the Route Vallon opposite the French Circle Sporting where he narrowly escaped arrest at the hands of the French Police who apprehended certain armed members of his body guard.
Following this incident and the failure of the attempt to capture the Chiho and the Chinese Police Stations he lay low for a time.
During the month of March 1916 he was again reported as being active and with Niau Tih Sung 鈕鐵生 planning a rising in the middle of the month referred to which did not materialise.
On March 24th an address through which he could be communicated with by his followers was No.33 Rue Admiral Bayle.
On May 18th at about 5 p.m. he was assassinated at No.14 Rue Chapel in the house of a Japanese named Yamada from whom he had rented an upstairs room which he had occupied and which, it was ascertained, he rarely left for about two months preceding the date of his death.
In consequence of information received this house was searched on one occasion by the French Police acting in conjunction with the Japanese Consular Authorities but Chen Che May happened to be absent at the time of the visit and so escaped.
It was known for some time before this event that money was being sent to Yamada from Seerang by Chinese and there was strong suspicion that these funds which were remitted by telegraph were for the purpose of financing the Revolutionaries.
The attention of the Consul General for Japan was called to this. He sent for Yamada and affected to be satisfied with the latter's explanation that the remittances were sent in connection with certain
page_data.zh:
副本。

10月14日

先生：

据警方报告，陈其美（Chen Che May）于1915年11月间在法租界活动。有人曾见他在已故王金发（Wang Ching Fah）的寓所，试图在那里借款三万美元。

1915年12月初，他住在瓦隆路（Route Vallon）法国总会体育场对面的一所房子里，险些被法国警察逮捕，当时法警抓获了他保镖中的几名武装人员。

在此事件以及袭击闸北和中国警察局未遂之后，他暂时隐匿起来。

1916年3月间，又有报告称他再次活跃，并与钮铁生（Niau Tih Sung）策划在该月中旬发动起义，但该计划并未实现。

3月24日，其追随者可通过贝勒路33号（No.33 Rue Admiral Bayle）与他联系。

5月18日下午5时许，他在霞飞路14号（No.14 Rue Chapel）一名叫山田（Yamada）的日本人的寓所内遇刺身亡。他从山田处租了一间楼上房间并一直居住，经查实，在死前约两个月内，他很少离开该处。

根据所得情报，法国警察曾联合日本领事当局对该住所进行过一次搜查，但陈其美恰好在访问期间外出，因而逃脱。

在此事发生前的一段时间里，众所周知有中国人从暹罗（Seerang）向山田汇款，人们强烈怀疑这些通过电报汇出的资金是用于资助革命党人。

此事已提请日本总领事注意。他传唤了山田，并对后者关于汇款是与南方商人进行某些

page_data.en:

commercial transactions which he had with merchants
in the South.
The Police obtained copies of two seals which
had been made by a Japanese engraver and handed
over to a representative of the Revolutionaries
in the French Concession on April 10th. These
were ordered by Chen Chi May.
One of the warrants which the Municipal Police
held for the arrest of Chen Chi May was countersigned
by the Consul General for Japan. It was not
operative in the French Concession as it did not
bear the seal of the French Consulate.
A letter was sent to Chen Chi May or to the
house which he occupied in August 1914 and another
was given to the Police to be given to him if he was
seen. It is worded as follows:-

"Council Room,
August 14th 1913.

"To General Chen Chi Mei.
You are hereby notified that you are not
permitted to remain in or enter the Foreign
Settlement of Shanghai.
If found within the limits of the Settlement
after receipt of this notice you will render
yourself liable to arrest by the Police.
By Order of the Council.
(sd) W.E. Laveson,
Secretary."

This document was not served upon him and it
is still in our possession.
In order to enable the Police to effect his
arrest legitimately if he was seen, a warrant was
applied for and issued on October 11th 1913 for being
in the Settlement contrary to the instructions
of the Consular Body.
This Warrant is still on file together with two
others one of which was issued at the request of

警方获取了两枚印章的副本，这些印章由一名日本雕刻师制作，并于4月10日移交给法租界的一名革命党代表。这些印章系陈其美（Chen Chi May）订购。

工部局警务处持有的逮捕陈其美（Chen Chi May）的逮捕令中，有一份由日本总领事副署。由于该逮捕令未加盖法国领事馆印章，因此在法租界无效。

1914年8月，曾有一封信寄给陈其美或他所居住的寓所，另一封信则交给警方，嘱其若见到陈其美便交给他。信件内容如下：

“会议室，
1913年8月14日。

致陈其美将军：

特此通知，您不得留在或进入上海外国租界。
若在收到本通知后仍被发现身处租界范围内，您将面临被警方逮捕的风险。

奉工部局之命。
（签名）W.E. Laveson，
秘书。”

此文件并未送达给他，目前仍由我方保管。

为了使警方在见到他时能够合法地实施逮捕，我方申请并于1913年10月11日签发了一份逮捕令，罪名是违反领事团的指令留在租界内。

该逮捕令连同另外两份仍存档在案，其中一份是应

the late Admiral Tseng on a charge of being connected
with the attempted Revolution of 1913 and the other
of which was issued at the instance of the Commissioner
of Foreign Affairs on a charge of being connected
with the Iron and Blood Association.
On October 31st I suggested issuing a Wanted Notice
and prepared a draft which is attached. It was not
approved of but instead instructions were given to
send a photograph of Chen Che May with a chit to
each senior detective. This was done.

Your Obedient Servant,

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.
